description: Rat cortical neurons cultured on electrode arrays received stimuli mixed from two hidden sources and self-organized to encode the two sources selectively. Changes in effective synaptic connectivity reduced variational free energy, and drugs that raised or lowered excitability disrupted the inference as a change in priors would.
limitations: One in vitro setting with a two-source blind separation task. The fit uses a reverse engineering method developed by the same group.
conflicts_of_interest: Karl Friston, the originator of the principle, is a co-author.

sources.quote: Upon receiving electrical stimuli—generated by mixing two hidden sources—neurons self-organised to selectively encode the two sources.
Pharmacological up- and downregulation of network excitability disrupted the ensuing inference, consistent with changes in prior beliefs about hidden sources.
